messages:
marie: FYI I hit a subtle DX issue in the Go sampleapp when a user aborts (close tab). the generator iterator keeps draining and the handler goroutine blocks. seems like we don't expose a clean client-side cancel.

marie: repro gist: 
```go
iter := client.Generator("tiny").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "summarize"})
for iter.Next() {
  if _, err := w.Write([]byte(iter.Text())); err != nil {
    // client disconnected; return but iterator keeps running elsewhere
    log.Println("write err", err)
    return
  }
}
```

diego: ah yeah we've seen variants. root cause often auth refresh / reconnect using a background ctx and the transport read loop not being force-closed.

toni: suggestion: add a Close(context.Context) on the iterator that cancels transport + read loop. semantics: idempotent, unblocks Next(), Err() yields ErrCanceled or ErrClosed. that makes handlers deterministic without cancelling whole request ctx.

marie: i like Close(ctx). can we also add a short cookbook entry in the README showing the pattern for HTTP handlers: attempt write -> on error call iter.Close(ctx) -> return. new devs frequently rely on Context.Background() hacks which hide the issue.

diego: implementation note: for HTTP transport we can call conn.Close(), for HTTP2/gRPC we should cancel the stream ctx. also guard against double-close on the event channel. unit test: create a fake server that keeps sending after Close and assert Next() returns within 100ms.

toni: +1. tiny API sketch: 
```go
type GeneratorIter interface {
  Next() bool
  Text() string
  Err() error
  Close(ctx context.Context) error // blocks until teardown or ctx done
}
```

marie: can docs-bot add an action item to audit sampleapps for Context.Background() in auth/refresh paths. we should update onboarding guide too.

ci-bot: CI: go-sdk-tests/streaming passed :white_check_mark:

diego: i'll open a draft PR with Close(ctx) + two sampleapp updates. i'll include the test harness and README snippet. tagging @marie @toni for review.
